summary:
ORBITAL EYE is an interactive astronomical data exploration platform that transforms SPHEREx space telescope observations into a visual journey across the infrared universe. It allows users to explore selected regions of the sky, retrieve available observations across different epochs and detectors, and visualize how celestial objects and their surroundings change over time.

By processing, aligning, and comparing multi-epoch infrared images, ORBITAL EYE helps users investigate potential motion and brightness variations in astronomical targets. The platform aims to make complex space telescope data more accessible through an intuitive interface, interactive visualizations, and scientific analysis tools.

Built around NASA’s SPHEREx mission data, ORBITAL EYE bridges the gap between raw astronomical observations and meaningful exploration, encouraging discovery, learning, and a deeper understanding of our dynamic universe.
details:
Project Details – ORBITAL EYE

What Does It Do?

ORBITAL EYE is an interactive astronomical exploration platform designed to make infrared space observations easier to access, visualize, and understand. Using data from NASA’s SPHEREx mission, the platform allows users to explore different regions of the sky and investigate how celestial objects appear across multiple observations taken at different times.

Our project focuses on five astronomical targets: Barnard’s Star, Epsilon Indi Ba/Bb, WISE 0855, RW Aurigae, and R Draconis. Users can explore available observations, compare images across different epochs and detectors, and investigate potential changes in an object's position or brightness.

How Does It Work?

The platform combines astronomical data retrieval, image processing, and interactive visualization into one workflow:

  1. Data Retrieval: Finds available SPHEREx observations for selected astronomical targets.
  2. Image Processing: Loads FITS astronomical images, handles image quality information, and prepares observations for comparison.
  3. Image Alignment: Uses World Coordinate System (WCS) information to align observations onto a common sky reference.
  4. Multi-Epoch Comparison: Enables users to examine observations from different dates and investigate possible changes over time.
  5. Scientific Exploration: Provides tools for image comparison, difference analysis, spectral exploration, and catalog-based investigation.

The goal is to turn complex astronomical datasets into a more understandable and interactive experience.

What Are Its Benefits and Intended Impact?

ORBITAL EYE makes publicly available astronomical data more approachable for students, researchers, and space enthusiasts. Instead of requiring users to manually download and process large scientific datasets, the platform brings important exploration and visualization capabilities into a unified interface.

Its intended impact includes:

  • Encouraging hands-on exploration of real NASA space telescope observations.
  • Supporting the investigation of celestial motion and brightness variability.
  • Making infrared astronomy more accessible to people without extensive experience in scientific data processing.
  • Demonstrating how open space data can support education, research, and scientific curiosity.

What Makes the Project Creative?

The creative aspect of ORBITAL EYE lies in combining astronomical image processing with an interactive, time-based exploration experience. Rather than treating each observation as an isolated image, the platform encourages users to compare observations across time and explore how the infrared sky changes.

It brings together data retrieval, image alignment, multi-epoch visualization, spectral tools, and catalog information in a single platform, creating a more engaging way to explore the universe.

Technologies and Tools Used

Backend:

  • Python
  • FastAPI
  • Astropy
  • Astroquery
  • NumPy
  • Photutils
  • Reproject

Frontend:

  • Next.js
  • React
  • TypeScript

Scientific Data and Processing:

  • NASA SPHEREx FITS observations
  • World Coordinate System (WCS)
  • Infrared image processing and analysis
  • Astronomical catalog resources

Factors Considered by Our Team

During development, we considered scientific accuracy, data quality, image alignment, missing or corrupted observations, and differences between observation dates and detectors. We also considered usability, performance, and the importance of presenting scientific results responsibly.

We recognize that preliminary image comparisons are not equivalent to confirmed astronomical discoveries. Therefore, the platform is designed to support further investigation while clearly acknowledging current data limitations and the need for additional validation.
